description: House win equals coin-in minus payout (integer cents)
explanation: 7117.0 machine-days have negative house win; these are valid outcomes and are kept.

description: Prepared view dollars equal source cents / 100
expected_relationship: usd == cents / 100 and hours == seconds / 3600, row by row
explanation: Confirms one conversion factor and no unit drift between layers.

description: property_day equals the sum of machine_day by gaming date
expected_relationship: daily property totals == sum over machines (source cents)
explanation: Validates the prepared property view against the source meters rather than against the other prepared view.

description: Availability within scheduled time within gaming day
expected_relationship: occupied <= available <= scheduled <= calendar day length; inactive rows carry no time or play
explanation: 0.0 active machine-days are shorter than the gaming day (install or retirement mid-day); exposure uses scheduled_seconds, not 24 h.

description: Active flag agrees with placements and install/retire dates
expected_relationship: active <=> a placement interval overlaps the gaming day; never active before install or after retirement
explanation: 1018 off-floor rows are excluded from all metrics (documented: 1,018).

description: Placement intervals are consistent and join 1:1
expected_relationship: no overlapping intervals per machine or per slot; interval join reproduces machine_day location/config with no fan-out
explanation: Interval join [effective_from_utc, effective_to_utc) is the only valid way to attach location history.

description: Money totals survive the location join (no duplication)
expected_relationship: coin-in after interval join == source coin-in
explanation: A naive machine_id join would overstate coin-in by $3,255,941.00; the pipeline uses the interval join only.

description: Theo equals coin-in x (1 - configured RTP)
expected_relationship: theo_cents == coin_in_cents x (1 - configured_rtp) per machine-day; luck residual == house win - theo
explanation: Theo is a deterministic function of wagers, so it is a luck-free demand measure. Realized win differs from theo by the luck residual.

description: Carded play is a strict subset and reconciles across machine meters, sessions and player_period
expected_relationship: carded <= all play per machine-day; sessions == machine_day carded columns; player_period total == sessions total
explanation: Carded play is 65.8% of all coin-in, so guest-level results describe tracked play only and are never scaled to all play.

description: Comp cost counted once: ledger cost == linked POS cogs, and is contained in POS cogs
expected_relationship: economic_cost_cents == linked cogs_cents; comp cost is a subset of pos_cogs; comp face value is not revenue
tolerance: exact cents per redemption; <= $0.01 per day
explanation: Contribution must subtract POS cogs once (comps included) and must not subtract comp cost a second time. Face value ($682,750) is menu price, not cost.

description: Supplied machine costs recompute from cost_rules
expected_relationship: lease/service/power per active machine-day and repair direct cost by gaming date of fault opening match the prepared view
explanation: Confirms the cost_rules interpretation used for contribution and for pricing downtime. Revenue-share lease = 20% of positive daily win.

description: Meter downtime reconciles to operations tickets
expected_relationship: scheduled - available (meters) ~= sum of ticket outage intervals clipped to the window
explanation: Ticket intervals can include time when a machine was not scheduled (e.g. install before first gaming day) or overlap; differences are reported, not forced.

description: Gaming days run 06:00-06:00 local and are contiguous
expected_relationship: 181 contiguous days; each starts at 06:00 Los Angeles time; only 2025-03-08 is 23 h
explanation: Exposure uses scheduled_seconds, so the DST day is not overstated by 1 h.

expected_relationship: net = payout - coin-in; residual = net + theo; contribution = -net + POS cash - POS cogs (comp cost not subtracted again)
explanation: Player tables use the opposite sign to machine tables.
